W2 (empirical), after E028. Tip is E027: 5.878 s, 0.7547 (20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30%, 8.75 true epochs, 219 steps at batch 2000). It clears the 0.753 bar by about 0.17 pp on seeds 0-2. The held-out margin is unmeasured.

Measured chain: E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E015 CUDA graphs 0.7574/6.58. E017 break-free 0.7537/6.548. E018 24/32 only 0.7502/5.99. E020 -1ep 0.7528/5.86. E021 group 2 at 320 0.7530/6.04. E023 -0.5ep 0.7538/6.198. E024 26px mid 0.7510/6.07. E025 EMA exponent 2 0.7557/6.20. E026 20px first phase 0.7540/6.017. E027 8.75 epochs 0.7547/5.878. E028 FreezeOut 0.7517/5.358.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch. Accuracy cost is 0.0-0.15 pp per 0.5 epoch (E020, E023, E027). It is the cheapest lever measured, and it is nearly free in the 3-seed view.
2. EMA gave +0.97 pp and Muon +0.66 pp. Both are already in the tip.
3. Time tracks pixel count and FLOPs, sublinearly on small maps. Early low resolution (E026) is nearly free. Dropping or shrinking the 28 px phase costs 0.3-0.5 pp.
4. Backward truncation (E028) saved 9% of time for a 0.3 pp drop on seeds 0-2. So compute cuts on the 32 px tail cost about 0.3 pp per 0.5 s, which is similar to or better than the epoch dial.
5. wd, label smoothing, Muon lr, LR floor and EMA exponent are flat within noise. E016's 0.7607 was noise.
6. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any edit that changes RNG use or the step count reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I again overpredicted time on E028 (predicted 5.8, measured 5.36) and on many earlier trims. Savings from trims are consistently larger than my model says, so I should shade time lower by 2-4% for compute cuts. Accuracy deltas under 0.3 pp are unreadable.

Unsure: the held-out 10-seed mean of the tip. Whether averaging or label-smoothing tweaks give anything. Whether per-sample loss tracking adds overhead in the compiled step.

forecasts.reason: Dropping 10% of samples is like a 0.9-epoch cut with extra bookkeeping. Time falls but accuracy likely lands below 0.753.
Time-neutral change. Any accuracy effect is within RNG noise.
Smoothing is flat elsewhere. The effect is hard to separate from noise.
Early low resolution is nearly free, so there is a small time gain and accuracy is about flat. The result is marginal against the bar.
Per-resolution whitening adds small prepare cost. It is unlikely to move accuracy beyond noise.

cruxes: What is the held-out seeds 3-12 mean of the E027 tip? If it is below 0.752, further trims are infeasible, and if it is above 0.754, trims can continue.
Does a 32 px tail compute cut (E028-style) cost less accuracy per second than the epoch dial once measured on held-out seeds?
Is per-sample loss tracking free inside the compiled and graph-captured step?
